The ranges encompass some of the most rugged and spectacular country in South Australia. Benbonyathe Hill, located on "The Plateau", is at 1,064 m (3,491 ft) the second highest point in the Flinders north of Wilpena Pound after Mount Hack. There are also several major mountains on the edge of the Gammon Ranges, two of which are actually higher the main range: Gammon Hill in the north, and Mount McKinlay dominating the south. The national park, declared in 1970, encompasses the former pastoral leases of Yankaninna and Balcanoona stations. Balcanoona Airport is within the park.
Vulkathunha-Gammon Ranges National Park is part of the Flinders Ranges geological successions, where abundant and diverse arrays of fossils show how animal life began on Earth over a period of 350 million years. These areas were submitted to the UNESCO World Heritage Centre for consideration as a World Heritage Site in April 2021, and as of August 2025 remain on the tentative list.
